newsitem.title: CANADA: De Gaulle statue vandalized in Quebec.
newsitem.headline: De Gaulle statue vandalized in Quebec.

text.p: A controversial statue honoring former French President Charles de Gaulle was vandalized with red paint early on Tuesday, police said.
The incident coincided with the 55th anniversary of the Second World War battle of Dieppe, where thousands of Canadian soldiers fought to liberate France from German occupation.
A message pasted on the base of the statue said in French: "Canadian blood in Dieppe. You should blush," followed by "Old bastard."
More than 900 Canadian soldiers died and 1,900 were captured at Dieppe on Aug. 9, 1942 one of the most tragic days of the war for Canada.
The De Gaulle statue sparked controversy in Quebec last month when it was unveiled 30 years years after the general's speech in 1967 in support of the French-speaking province's independence.
"Vive le Quebec libre" (Long Live a Free Quebec) de Gaulle proclaimed to an ecstatic crowd from the balcony of Montreal's City Hall. His words sparked a diplomatic storm between Canada and France.
In Quebec City, the statue of de Gaulle stands in front of the Plains of Abraham, a grassy park overlooking the St. Lawrence river where British troops defeated the French in 1759.
Quebec City police said they had no suspects in the vandalism of the statue, which is usually kept under close surveillance.
"No suspect has been identified and no witness is known," police spokesman Lyne Jacques told Reuters.
